Senses.Note: The corpus does not reduce the word to one theoretical proposition. It asks about the teaching-body's function (法身用) and "the matter beyond the teaching-body" (法身向上事). The Old Venerables Record says "the teaching-body also has two kinds of illness" (法身亦有兩般病): reaching it while attachment to the standard remains, with one's own view still present and sitting at its side, is the first. Another raised saying states that "the teaching-body speaks" (法身說法). These predicates differ, but every witness still designates the same teaching-body rather than a second lexical referent.

Senses.Explanation: The teaching-body is a corpus-defined body or person-shaped referent whose predicates vary across direct explanations rather than collapsing to an imported glossary formula. Chan records define it through a person enlarging the Way, originally present nature, formless responsiveness, activities, and deliberately concrete answers. Qianyan places three word explanations together: a robe displays the teaching and so is a "teaching-robe" (法衣); "a person can enlarge the Way, therefore it is called teaching-body" (人能宏道，故謂之法身); and being everywhere and clear is called the "teaching-eye" (法眼). Other records give deliberately different predicates. Weilin calls it "each person's originally present own nature" (當人本有之自性). Huanglong says, "the teaching-body has no form; responding to things, it manifests form" (法身無相。應物現形), then raises his whisk and calls that the teaching-body before laughing. Lishan answers the question with "a flower in the sky, a heat shimmer" (空華陽𦔨). Xiyuan Daan answers it by repeating that "all activities are the teaching-body's function" (一切施為，盡是法身用).
